question.text: The current density in a cylindrical wire of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The current through the outer portion of the wire between radial distances <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>π</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Current density is defined as current per unit cross-section area. Therefore,

i=JA=J×πR2-R24

⇒i=4×106×π×16×10-6×34

⇒i=48π A
